A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional appendix J in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on eigenspace prediction, parametric PDEs, iterative solvers and optimal control, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds grid-transfer, smoothness, LOBPCG and sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 and appendix F.6 add a hybrid inference procedure: solve the eigenproblem in the predicted subspace and use its solution to initialize LOBPCG. The underlying neural architecture, subspace losses, embedding technique and stabilization remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix F.4 adds a discretization-transfer scenario: a one-dimensional quantum-mechanics model trained on 100 grid points is evaluated on grids with 150–500 points. The physical dataset families and other tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The new LOBPCG experiment compares initialization from subspace regression against random initialization (Table 10 and Figure 7). Existing comparator sets are retained; changing the Table 3–4 labels from QR/stochastic to L1/L2 does not introduce new methods.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the evaluation design with transfer across grid resolutions, three smoothness measures evaluated over 1,000 random feature pairs, and learned-versus-random LOBPCG initialization with a 1,000-iteration cap. Appendix J also introduces retraining on randomized train/test splits. These are additional protocols, while the original benchmark settings largely remain intact.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's embedding-size studies and geometric illustration, v3 tests whether trained networks actually learn smoother mappings using three indicators (F.5), evaluates robustness to finer discretizations (F.4), and examines split and hyperparameter sensitivity (J). These add substantial mechanistic and robustness evidence.

E5.justification: v1 already reports ranges across three selected grid-search configurations and timing variability. v3 adds five random train/test splits with means and standard deviations for elliptic and Burgers experiments (Table 14), plus test-set dispersion for LOBPCG (Table 10). It explicitly identifies the main results as single-run metrics; the repeated-split study does not cover every comparison.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables and plotted results are retained, but substantial new results appear in F.4–F.6 and J. For example, new Table 6 reports errors of 0.83% at 100 points and 6.79% at 500 points. New Table 10 reports 263 mean LOBPCG iterations with a 40-dimensional learned initialization versus 685 with random initialization for k1=k2. Smoothness and variability findings are also added.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the missing multiplication by psi in the Schrodinger equation (3) and defines the smoothness indicators in equations (49)–(51). The main theorems and appendix proofs retain their substance. However, new prose in Section 3.1 incorrectly makes equal column spaces necessary for zero loss, contradicting the retained subspace-inclusion criterion.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about subspace regression, invariant losses, embedding, theoretical justification and applications. The added experiments support these claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes the smoothness theorem's existence result from evidence about trained networks and interprets the new angular measurements as averaging information across target subspaces. It also discusses practical grid-transfer accuracy and argues that hyperparameter sensitivity exceeds split variability. The original limitations concerning inefficient learned representations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F.2 newly documents searching architectures on a 32×32 grid and retraining the three best configurations on 100×100. This is additional disclosure, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun. The repository link already appeared in v1; its relocation to the new reproducibility statement does not establish changed code availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Knyazev's LOBPCG reference and positions subspace regression as an initializer for a classical iterative eigensolver. The remaining related-work coverage and central novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized clarifications and notation edits, revises author affiliations, adds explanatory footnotes, and introduces a reproducibility section and new experimental subsections. Most existing prose, the main section sequence and the conclusion remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds dedicated displays for grid transfer, smoothness, LOBPCG performance and variability (Tables 6–10 and 14–15), plus a two-panel LOBPCG convergence figure. Existing figures and tables are retained with changes in placement, sizing and numbering; Tables 3–4 also adopt explicit loss-function labels.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for v1's embedding rationale through measurements on trained networks and adds useful grid-transfer, LOBPCG and split-sensitivity checks. These improve validation and practical guidance, although repeated-split evidence covers only selected models and tasks. The new, incorrect equal-column-space explanation in Section 3.1 is a localized regression. The evidence and reporting gains outweigh this flaw, yielding a limited net improvement.
